D: A London bookshop owner falls for the most famous film star in the world.
P: Serve dessert when the dinner party guests compete for the last brownie.
S: the Portobello Road market outside William's shop
Crusty bread with brie, ham and chutney cut into small sandwiches, with a bowl of olives.

Shortbread of butter, sugar, flour and rice flour, baked at 160C for 25 minutes, cut into fingers. Beat 250g soft butter with 110g caster sugar until pale. Sift in 280g plain flour, 70g rice flour and a pinch of salt and mix to a dough. Press into a lined 20 x 30cm tin, prick all over with a fork and chill 15 minutes. Bake at 160C for 25 to 30 minutes until pale golden. Sprinkle with caster sugar and cut into fingers while warm, then cool in the tin. Serve with a pot of tea.
Thick white bread buttered and filled with cheddar, tomato and pickle relish, toasted in a pan until golden, cut into quarters.
M: Honey's birthday dinner at Max and Bella's
Chicken thighs braised with white wine, mushrooms and tarragon, finished with cream, served with mash and green beans.
Ritz lemon dill salmon and asparagus

Salmon fillets roasted on lemon slices with dill and butter at 200C for 12 minutes, with crushed potatoes and asparagus. Halve 600g baby potatoes and boil 15 minutes until tender, then crush lightly with 30g butter, salt and chopped dill. Lay 2 lemons' worth of slices on a lined tray and sit 4 salmon fillets on top. Dot with 20g butter, scatter with dill and season. Roast at 200C for 12 minutes. Add 2 bunches asparagus tossed in oil for the last 6 minutes. Serve with the crushed potatoes and a lemon wedge.
W: the last brownie at Honey's birthday dinner
Fudgy chocolate brownies baked at 170C for 25 minutes, cut into squares, the last one kept aside for the saddest story.
K: William spilling orange juice all over Anna

Freshly squeezed orange juice topped with cold sparkling wine in flutes, a twist of orange on the rim. Best kept in the glass. Squeeze 6 oranges to get about 400ml juice and strain. Chill the juice and a 750ml bottle of sparkling wine well. Pour 100ml orange juice into each of 4 flutes, then slowly top with sparkling wine. Twist a strip of orange peel over each and hang it on the rim. For non-drinkers, top with sparkling water instead.

s.note: the Portobello Road market outside William's shop
s.how: Split a loaf of crusty bread and fill with sliced brie, ham and a spread of tomato chutney. Cut into small pieces and pin with toothpicks. Serve on a board with a bowl of green olives, like lunch from a market stall.

Butter thick white bread on the outside. Fill with sliced cheddar, tomato and a spoon of pickle relish. Toast in a pan over medium heat until golden and melting, pressing down. Cut into quarters. Simple enough even for a flatmate.

m.note: Honey's birthday dinner at Max and Bella's
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden. Pour in 250ml white wine and simmer 20 minutes, then stir in 200ml cream and chopped tarragon. Serve with mashed potato and green beans at a small birthday dinner.

w.note: the last brownie at Honey's birthday dinner
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour and 2 tbsp cocoa. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes. Cut into squares and keep the very last one aside for whoever tells the saddest story.
